newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Pertamina sees oil price firm in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Pertamina sees oil price firm in 1996.

text.p: The director of Indonesia's state oil company, Baharuddin, predicted on Wednesday that oil prices would continue to be strong through the end of 1996 as the northern hemisphere winter approached.
"Oil prices are currently already strong. I think the price will continue firm through the end of the year as the winter season is approaching," Baharuddin told Reuters.
"Oil demand usually increases during the winter. This is very positive for Indonesia," he said.

"Indonesia will receive around $600 million for every one dollar increase above the price envisaged in the budget. However, 47 percent of this will be swallowed by the purchase of crude to feed our own refineries. But we are still in surplus," he said.
Indonesia had set a price of $16.50 a barrel in its 1996/97 (April-March) budget.
"Indonesia's oil price average is $19.44 in the period April-September. We are exporting around 760,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude," Baharuddin said.
Indonesia, the only Asian OPEC member, currently produces about 1.60 million bpd of crude oil and condensate.
